design_rationale: Participants were explicitly randomized after baseline assessment using block randomization stratified by gender and motivation to quit into the SC or ME treatment conditions.

domain_judgments.rationale: Block randomization with stratification was reported and most baseline variables were balanced, but the method used to generate the sequence and allocation concealment were not described, and age differed between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were then randomized (using block randomization to ensure stratification by gender and level of motivation to quit smoking...) into one of two treatment conditions.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and intervention staff necessarily knew the behavioral treatment received, but fidelity and contamination were monitored, treatment delivery differed as intended, and the primary effect was analyzed by randomized assignment using ITT.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Results revealed that ME content delivered to those in the ME condition was appropriate, and that it exceeded significantly that delivered to SC participants (P < 0.001).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessments were missing for 48%, 38%, and 28% of randomized participants at 2, 4, and 6 months, respectively, and coding every missing participant as a smoker does not establish that the effect estimate is unbiased when missing outcomes may differ from observed outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Although 2-month follow-up data were collected from only 52% of participants... participation rates rose to 62% at the 4-month follow-up... and to 72% at the 6-month follow-up.

domain_judgments.rationale: Smoking abstinence was measured identically in both groups using self-report with biochemical verification, discrepant results were conservatively classified as smoking, and follow-up assessors were blinded to assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Follow-up assessments were administered by research staff blinded to participant intervention assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: A clinical-trial registration was identified and the main outcome and follow-up times were clearly reported, but no protocol or prespecified analysis plan is provided to verify that choices among available-case versus ITT analyses, time points, and subgroup or utilization analyses were made before examining results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Results presented in this manuscript consist of analysis of 2-month, 4-month and 6-month assessments, presented separately by follow-up.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because substantial missing outcome data at every follow-up create a high risk of bias despite balanced attrition between arms and the missing-equals-smoking ITT convention. Unreported sequence generation/allocation concealment and limited evidence about prespecification add some concerns.

design_rationale: This was an explicitly randomized two-arm parallel-group trial using stratified block randomization with randomly selected block sizes and centralized sequence generation by an independent data manager.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence used stratified random blocks, was generated and centrally implemented by an independent data manager on a secure server, and the groups were balanced at baseline, supporting adequate sequence generation and concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was centralized with an independent data manager who generated and uploaded the randomization sequence onto a secure server at the Albert Einstein College of Medicine.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and the study coordinator were unblinded in this behavioral trial, the intervention provided somewhat greater attention and reminders than control, and patch uptake differed numerically between arms, although both arms were offered patches and the primary analysis followed intention-to-treat principles.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The two study conditions were not perfectly “attentionmatched” with one fewer module in the AHA control and reminders sent only to the PSFW+ participants who were due to visit the site.

domain_judgments.rationale: A substantial 25.3% were lost to follow-up and were assumed to be smoking in the ITT analysis; this conservative convention is common in cessation trials but does not establish that missingness was unrelated to the true outcome or balanced by arm.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The ITT approach assumed participants lost to follow-up (n=128; 25.3%) were non-abstinent.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary abstinence outcome was generally measured identically with self-report and biochemical verification by blinded assessors, but eight self-reported abstinent participants lacked contemporaneous biochemical verification because of COVID-19 and were accepted as abstinent, creating some measurement uncertainty.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: For the n=8 who reported abstinence during the COVID-19 research visit ban and lacked biochemical verification, we accepted their self-report as evidence of abstinence.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered and the primary outcome and ITT strategy were described as pre-planned, but the provided report does not establish availability of a prespecified statistical analysis plan, and multiple cutoffs, time points, outcome definitions, and adjusted analyses leave some potential for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The pre-planned primary trial outcome was biochemically confirmed 7-day point-prevalence abstinence at 6-months post-enrollment utilizing intention-to-treat (ITT) (i.e., lost to followup assumed non-abstinent) strategy.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged some concerns. Randomization was robust, but concerns remain because participants were unblinded with unequal intervention attention, 25.3% lacked follow-up outcomes, several abstinence outcomes lacked contemporaneous biochemical verification, and complete prespecification of all reported analyses was not demonstrated.

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that 474 enrolled participants were randomized to usual care or the cell phone intervention using adaptive randomization.

domain_judgments.rationale: Adaptive randomization and good balance on most measured baseline factors support a random process, but allocation concealment is not described and age differed significantly between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Adaptive randomization was used to ensure treatment group balance with respect to several important participant characteristics (i.e., depression history, number of cigarettes per day, and nicotine dependence).

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and intervention personnel necessarily knew assignment, the intervention created substantially greater contact, and completion declined across counseling calls, although an intention-to-treat analysis retained all randomized participants.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: An intent-to-treat approach was used in which participants who did not complete the 3-month follow-up were coded as smokers.

domain_judgments.rationale: The number completing the 3-month assessment and reasons for missingness by group are not reported; coding all missing participants as smokers retains the randomized sample but does not establish that missingness could not bias the effect.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: An intent-to-treat approach was used in which participants who did not complete the 3-month follow-up were coded as smokers.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were collected consistently using ACASI and one abstinence measure was biochemically verified, but the primary outcome was self-reported and participants were aware of treatment assignment, which could influence reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome of interest was self-reported 7-day point prevalence abstinence at the time of the 3-month follow-up.

domain_judgments.rationale: The paper identifies a primary outcome and reports several prespecified-looking smoking outcomes, but no preregistration or analysis protocol is reported to rule out selection among multiple outcome definitions or analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Other smoking status variables of interest included biochemically verified 24-hr abstinence, 30-day abstinence, and continuous abstinence.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. The main uncertainties are unreported allocation concealment and follow-up completeness, lack of blinding for self-reported outcomes, differential intervention contact and adherence, and absence of reported preregistration or a prespecified analysis plan; no domain clearly warrants a high-risk judgment.

design_rationale: The study explicitly reports stratified random allocation by a computer algorithm in a 1:1:1 parallel-group design.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated stratified sequence was used, but allocation concealment was not described and several statistically significant baseline imbalances were observed, although these may have arisen by chance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Then, within those strata, they were randomized via computer algorithm to one of three conditions in 1:1:1 fashion into a parallel group design.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants necessarily knew whether they received counseling, Internet treatment, or self-help, intervention uptake was incomplete, adherence to NRT was not directly measured, and the analysis used observed outcomes rather than a clearly described intention-to-treat strategy, though no intervention-related deviations were explicitly reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The mean number of counseling sessions attended was 3.6 out of 6 (or 60%), and the mean number of visits to the CBI Web site was 3.2.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome retention fell to 81% at 52 weeks, and missingness was demonstrably associated with abstinence; adjustment using completer status does not establish that estimates were unbiased under outcome-dependent missingness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: As results indicated that the missingness was not completely at random (i.e., completers were more likely to be abstinent), we used a mixed-effects nonlinear regression model.

domain_judgments.rationale: Smoking abstinence was measured consistently across groups using a prespecified self-report definition with carbon-monoxide verification, making differential measurement bias unlikely despite participants' awareness of assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were coded as abstinent only if they reported no cigarette use, not even a puff, in the last 7 days and if their CO level was ≤10 ppm.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified analysis plan is reported, and several abstinence definitions, time points, secondary outcomes, candidate covariates, and data-dependent covariate selection created scope for selective reporting or analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Prior to the final analysis, we used a multivariate model to test a set of candidate covariates for their relationship to the outcome and retained variables with a p-value < .10 for inclusion in the final model.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven primarily by outcome-dependent missingness with only 81% retained at 52 weeks and no analysis clearly demonstrating robustness to this missingness. Additional concerns involve unreported allocation concealment, incomplete intervention uptake without a clearly described intention-to-treat analysis, and analytic/reporting flexibility.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly allocated 1:1 using a computer-driven randomization algorithm, with concealment from the research assistant and investigative team and stratification by site, motivation to quit, and race.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated, concealed from recruiters and investigators, stratified on prespecified factors, and produced groups balanced on nearly all measured baseline characteristics.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Candidates who met these criteria... were randomized in a 1:1 schedule... using a computer-driven randomization algorithm that was concealed from the research assistant and the investigative team.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants necessarily knew whether they received intensive group therapy, intervention uptake was limited, nicotine-patch use differed between arms at three months, and some controls reported contamination, although the primary analysis followed intention-to-treat principles and intervention fidelity was high.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary analyses used an intent-to-treat strategy, and participants who were not evaluable at the 6-month timepoint were treated as nonabstinent.

domain_judgments.rationale: Six-month outcome ascertainment was incomplete and somewhat lower in the intervention arm, and the authors stated that missingness might not be random; classifying missing participants as smokers is conservative but does not eliminate all possible bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The PSF group analytic sample included 176 participants (81.5%) evaluable for the primary study outcome... and the control group sample was 196 (86.7%).

domain_judgments.rationale: Smoking abstinence was measured identically in both groups using a prespecified self-report question with objective exhaled-carbon-monoxide verification, reducing scope for bias from participant awareness of assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A negative response to this question and exhaled carbon monoxide (ECO) level of <10 parts per million... constituted biochemically verified 7-day point-prevalence abstinence.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome and time point were clearly identified and reported, but no preregistered protocol or statistical analysis plan is presented to rule out selective choice among numerous secondary outcomes and analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was biochemically confirmed, 7-day point-prevalence abstinence at 6 months.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns. Randomization and objective outcome measurement were strong, but incomplete outcome ascertainment, limited intervention uptake and contamination/co-intervention differences, and lack of reported preregistration leave plausible residual bias.

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that eligible patients were randomly allocated via a trial website to usual care or the combined app and carbon-monoxide self-monitoring intervention.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was explicitly randomized through a trial website and observed baseline differences were generally compatible with chance in this small trial, but the sequence-generation method and concealment safeguards were not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: randomly allocated during biannual cohort visits patients smoking ≥3 cigarettes a day via a trial website

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and care providers could not be blinded, uptake of the assigned intervention was very low, and nicotine-replacement therapy differed between groups, so substantial deviations and co-interventions could affect outcomes despite use of an intention-to-treat analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Eleven (26%) of the participants in the intervention group sent at least one result of a CO measurement with the Smokerlyzer App... Twelve (28.5%) participants in the intervention group reported using the Stop-tabac.ch app multiple times a week during the first month of the intervention.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 3 of 81 participants were lost to follow-up, and the prespecified intention-to-treat analysis conservatively counted missing smoking outcomes as smoking.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients with missing data or a positive CO breath test at 6 months of follow-up were counted as smokers.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome combined a defined self-report measure with biochemical CO verification applied across groups, but nurses conducting verification and treating physicians collecting self-reports were not blinded and could potentially influence ascertainment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was the combination of selfreported continuous abstinence biochemically verified at 6 months by an in-person CO... that was done by nurses not blinded for treatment status.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered and the primary and secondary outcomes and analyses are described, but the protocol or prespecified statistical analysis plan was not provided for comparison, leaving some uncertainty about selective reporting among adjusted analyses and outcome definitions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The trial protocol was approved by Swiss Ethics and registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, ID NCT02840513.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because intervention adherence was very poor and co-intervention use differed between groups in an unblinded behavioral trial, creating high risk from deviations from intended interventions. Additional concerns arise from incompletely reported randomization safeguards, unblinded outcome assessment, and limited information for excluding selective reporting.

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that 158 participants were randomized among three intervention arms, with randomization stratified by baseline cigarettes per day.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although allocation was explicitly randomized and stratified, the method used to generate the sequence and whether allocation was concealed were not reported, and there was a moderate baseline housing imbalance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was stratified by number of cigarettes smoked per day at baseline (5–10 and [10 cigarettes/- day).

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants necessarily knew whether they received text messages and counseling, intervention exposure was incomplete, and the extent to which deviations affected outcomes is unclear, although analyses used an intention-to-treat approach and counseling fidelity was monitored.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: On average, participants in the SC?TM?ABT arm completed 4.25 of the seven counseling sessions (data not shown; n = 51, SD = 2.42).

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 72.2% were retained at 12 weeks; missing participants were conservatively classified as nonadherent and non-abstinent, but this assumption may bias effects if missingness differed by true outcome, despite similar retention across arms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The overall retention rate was 72.2 % at 12 weeks. There was no difference in retention across treatment groups at any time point.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were defined and measured consistently across groups using pill counts for adherence and carbon-monoxide verification for self-reported abstinence, limiting assessor influence despite lack of blinding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Self-reported 7-day point prevalence smoking abstinence was verified by a carbon monoxide (CO) \8 ppm and measured at 1, 4, 8, and 12 weeks.

domain_judgments.rationale: A trial registration is identified, but no prespecified protocol or analysis plan is provided for comparison, while multiple time points, pairwise comparisons, and models were analyzed without multiplicity adjustment, allowing possible selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Significance tests, including comparisons between specific treatment arms, were made without adjustments to p-values.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns, driven by absent details on sequence generation and allocation concealment, substantial missing follow-up handled by failure imputation, incomplete intervention exposure, and potential selective reporting across multiple outcomes and analyses. Outcome measurement itself was objective and consistent across groups.
